tor active — your code is ready
Testing only — a code shared this way (message, email) skips the in-person check a QR scan gives you. Anyone who intercepts it could pair as this contact.
Both devices scan each other. The code carries your reachable address and keys — no account, no phone number, nothing else.

Allow camera access in system settings to take a photo.

Your packets for this chat are deleted from the nodes after this time, at the latest after 24 hours. Shorter means fewer traces; your contact must pick them up within that time. Applies to what you send.
Messages are stored only in RAM and wiped when the screen locks
first message on mobile data can take a few minutes

Active — this chat\'s outgoing traffic uses only this node.
Registered, not yet confirmed — sending on both the standard nodes and this one until the first message gets through.

Scan a QR code to add a contact

Send your current connection info so they keep reaching you reliably.
Tor connection state and GRAL security overview
Alongside the PIN, not instead of it — can only unlock normally, never the panic PIN. Off by default.
The identity your own QR code shows to a NEW contact. Renewing it doesn\'t affect contacts you\'ve already paired with.
For networks that block Tor (e.g. certain countries/providers)

Optional: paste your own bridge lines (one per line). They always win over the automatic connection. Get them from bridges.torproject.org or the Telegram bot @GetBridgesBot. obfs4, Snowflake and plain IP:Port bridges are supported.
If the network blocks Tor, the app tries other ways by itself. Nothing to set up.
No way found yet. The app tries again in a few minutes.
Company bridge saved (%1$d line(s)). Tried first when Tor is blocked.

Off: never used. Auto: best-effort store-and-forward mailbox — used only when a contact can\'t be reached directly, or proactively for transfers over 2 MB. Mandatory: every message routes through the relay, LAN/Tor-direct skipped entirely — meant for testing the relay path, switch freely. Off by default.
or paste the connection string shown by the relay
Tried in order if the primary relay above is unreachable. Both are shared with new contacts in your QR code, so they can reach you even when one relay is down. Leave empty if you don\'t have any.
Paste a signed relay list from your organization to fill the backup relay above automatically. Re-importing an updated list replaces the previous one.

Add your own unpruuf Node-Mesh server(s) — see node-mesh-server/README.md. Only you can write to your own node. Scan one node per server, the app fetches the other nodes of that server itself. Every new contact gets its own nodes from this pool, up to %1$d in total.
This node moved to a new address — every paired Business Node-Mesh contact will be notified automatically.
or paste the string shown by your node on first start
Your own QR code will show a new identity from now on. Contacts you\'ve already paired with are unaffected — they already run on their own per-contact identity, exchanged once right after pairing.
YOUR SAFETY NUMBER FOR THIS CONTACT
Compare this with %1$s over a call or voice message — NOT the same channel you used to share the pairing code. If both sides see the same number, the pairing code wasn\'t tampered with on the way.
Which side\'s relay list is used to reach %1$s. Automatic switches on its own rhythm; pin it manually to force one side.
Codes don\'t match. Do not assume this contact is who they claim — ask them to read their code again, or re-pair carefully.
This version of unpruuf is more than 6 months old and no longer runs. Please install the latest update.
This device appears to be rooted

unpruuf refuses to run on a rooted device. Root access lets an attacker read app memory, extract keys, and bypass screenshot protection directly — no app-layer defense can close that gap, so unpruuf doesn\'t try to run with it open. Nothing has been started: no keys generated, no connection made.
Un-root this device, or install unpruuf on a device that isn\'t rooted, and try again.
unpruuf %1$s needs a license code to run. Paste the code you received from your reseller below.
The license for this device (%1$s) expired on %2$s. Enter a renewal code to continue.
Enter a valid license code to continue.
%1$d of your nodes are offline until you unlock this server. Unlock only if YOU (or your provider) restarted it.

This sends your owner key to the server so it can bring its nodes back online under the same addresses.\n\nDo this only if you know why it restarted. If the server may have been taken or copied, do NOT unlock — set up a new server instead.
Server unlocked. Its nodes are coming back online.
Unlock failed — server not reachable or the key was refused.
Your report has been handed over. As soon as the reporting office confirms receipt, your case number appears here. You don\'t need to do anything.
Changes from the reporting office appear here automatically. Your case number is only for you: it helps you refer to your report, it is not needed to log in.
Scan your organisation\'s QR code. You only do this once — no name, no phone number, no account.
This is not a reporting-office code.
This code belongs to another app, not to a reporting office.
The code\'s connection address looks invalid. Ask the reporting office for a new code.
This code comes from an outdated version. Ask the reporting office for a new code.
Start a new case with the + button. Each case is separate: the reporting office cannot tell that two cases come from the same phone.
All messages and keys of this case are deleted from this phone. The reporting office keeps the case. You will no longer be able to read replies to it on this phone.
Import a server\'s node list from its setup page, rename or delete lists.
A list is a group of your own nodes, for example one server or one customer. When you add a contact you choose one list, and the contact gets three nodes from it.
No lists yet. Import the file from your server\'s setup page, or add a node by QR under Settings → Business Node-Mesh.
Choose the file you saved from the server\'s setup page (\"Liste als Datei speichern\"). Room for %1$d more nodes.
The file contains your write key for the server. Move it only to your own phone and delete it afterwards.
%1$d nodes in the file, %2$d of them new on this device.
The list and its %1$d nodes are removed from this device. The servers themselves are not touched.
The list and its %1$d nodes are removed from this device. %2$d contact(s) use nodes from it and will no longer reach you.
The QR you show carries three nodes from the list you pick above.

A company can keep your node lists up to date. Paste the feed code you got from them. The app finds the feed itself (its address changes every few hours) and only accepts lists that really come from the company.
The feed code is a secret from your company. Do not pass it on.
The app stops following this feed. The lists it filled stay on this device until you delete them.
A group exists only on your phone and on the phones of its members. Agree on a group with your team, then everyone creates it with the same code.
Group messages that were not shown
%1$s wrote to a group you have not created on this phone.
%1$s wrote to one of your groups but is not a member in your list.
Not a valid code. Check for typing mistakes.
The code cannot be changed. It is what makes this the same group on every phone.
One person creates the code and tells the others (read it out or send it in an existing chat). Everybody creates the group with the same code and picks the same people from their own contacts.
You have no contacts yet. Add the group members first.
Every member must know every other member. Only people who also picked this group with the same code will see your messages here.
The group and its messages are removed from this phone only. The other members keep theirs until they remove it too.
No messages. Messages disappear from this phone a few minutes after they are shown, like in every chat.
%1$s has %2$d people in this group, you have %3$d. Messages may not reach everyone. Compare the member lists.
That is not a valid feed code, or this feed is already added.
Feed added. Fetching the current lists…
Feed removed. The lists it filled stay until you delete them.
That is not a node list. Use the file from the server\'s setup page (\"Liste als Datei speichern\").
Not imported: needs room for %1$d more nodes, only %2$d free (limit %3$d). Delete a list you no longer use first.
List deleted, %1$d node(s) removed from this device.
Invalid QR code: Tor wasn\'t ready on the other device. Reopen the QR screen there and scan again.
This QR code is from an older app version. Update both devices and scan again.

This contact\'s key has changed since you last paired with them. If they reinstalled or reset the app, re-verify their safety number before trusting this. To replace them, delete the old contact first.

This QR code\'s node address looks invalid. Ask them to check their node setup and try again.

This code was already used for one contact. Close and reopen this screen to pair the next one — every contact gets its own keys and nodes.
Choose a node list for this contact first — the QR you show carries three nodes from it.

Backup relay saved — used if the primary is unreachable.
Both backup relays saved — tried in order if the primary is unreachable.
Pairing identity renewed. Existing contacts are unaffected — this only changes your own QR code going forward.

Use this phone as the Temp Node

This phone becomes the Temp Node for this chat only, with a new address that exists only while it runs. Your contact can pick up your messages only while this phone is on, awake and online. When you stop it, the address and everything still waiting on it are gone, and the chat uses your normal servers again.
Keep the app open and the phone online. If the app is closed or the phone goes off, nothing waits for your contact.
